1	# Task 2: forest of 10,000 instances
2	
3	Build a scene with Aura3D (`@aura3d/engine`, already installed in node_modules).
4	
5	Requirements:
6	1. A ground plane and exactly 10,000 scattered objects drawn with instancing (not 10,000 separate meshes): 8,000 trees (a trunk and a canopy, each instanced) and 2,000 rocks.
7	2. Placement is deterministic from a fixed seed (same forest every load), no overlaps needed.
8	3. Per-instance colour variation (canopies and rocks do not all share one colour).
9	4. One directional light that casts shadows, and exponential fog.
10	5. The camera slowly orbits the forest and the whole scene is visible.
11	
12	The rendering contract in the next section applies.
13	
14	## Rendering contract (all tasks)
15	
16	- Draw into the existing `<canvas id="app">` (640x360 CSS pixels, device pixel ratio 1). Do not resize it or create another canvas.
17	- Render continuously with `requestAnimationFrame`. When the first frame has been drawn set `window.__EVAL_READY__ = true`.
18	- No network access: load assets only from `/assets/...` (served from `public/assets`). Do not import from CDNs.
19	- Code goes in `src/` (TypeScript, strict). The entry is `src/main.ts`. It must pass `typecheck` and build with `vite build`.
20	- When you are done, call `finish`.
21

I'm sizing up the scene: a ground plane roughly 170-200 units wide with a forest radius around 60-70, exponential fog matching the background color to hide the horizon, and a simple shadow setup with centered fit and high-resolution mapping. For the camera, I'm placing it at a distance of 105 with height 70, aimed slightly above ground level with a 45-degree field of view.

I'm checking that the camera distance and fog density keep the forest's full width visible without clipping — settling on radius 85, height 55, and a fog density of 0.004. For the forest itself, I'm populating it with 8,000 trees (each a trunk cylinder plus a canopy cone) and 2,000 rock spheres, varying tree scale slightly for natural variation. I'm also planning to set a ready flag right after the first animation frame and update the camera pose each frame with cut set to true to avoid unwanted smoothing.

input.summary: I wrote src/main.ts. It typechecks, but I haven't run it in a browser or run `vite build`, so the rendering is unchecked. The scene is a ground plane plus exactly 10,000 instanced objects: 8,000 trunks (cylinders) and 8,000 canopies (cones), which make up the 8,000 trees, and 2,000 rocks (squashed spheres). That is 18,000 instances across 3 draws, since each tree's trunk and canopy are separate instances. A fixed-seed LCG places everything on a disc of radius 62, so the forest is the same on every load. Canopies and rocks get per-instance HSL colours, and trunks share one brown. There is one directional light with shadows (4096 map, fitted to the forest) and exponential fog (`effects.fog` with mode "exp"). A hemisphere light and a neutral environment add fill. The camera orbits slowly at radius 88 and height 58, using `app.camera.setPose` each frame, and the whole forest is in view. `window.__EVAL_READY__` is set after the first frame is drawn. That flag fires two animation frames after the first `onFrame` callback, which assumes the engine draws that frame in between.
